ariyipp links two phones over end-to-end encrypted FCM to relay SMS between them: a companion phone (with the SIM) forwards its incoming SMS to your main device, where you read and reply to them as a chat, and the main device can send SMS back through the companion. Notification capture and webhook posting are optional extras. This device\'s role is shown below, and can be switched anytime.

ariyipp v1.0 - Pair two phones over end-to-end encrypted FCM to relay SMS between them. The main device receives the relayed SMS as a searchable chat and can reply; the companion phone (with the SIM) forwards its incoming SMS and sends SMS on request. Pick a role on first run and switch anytime. Optional extras: notification capture to a webhook, encrypted backup and restore, per-conversation mute, and a liveness heartbeat that warns if the other device goes offline. Bring your own Firebase project (BYO-FCM).
1. Tap “Grant notification access” and enable ariyipp in the system list - this lets the app see notifications.\n2. Tap “Ignore battery optimization” so it runs reliably in the background.

Enter your Webhook URL and the auth token. The token is sent as a header: by default “Authorization: Bearer <token>”. For a custom Header Auth credential, set the Auth header name to “key” and clear the prefix so the raw token is sent. Tap the eye icon to reveal the token. Use an https URL - content is sensitive.
Under “Included apps”, tap “Choose apps” to pick which apps to capture. If you select none, all apps are captured. Selecting apps limits capture to just those.

Settings → “Keywords & notes” lists every app you selected under Apps. Against each app you can set:

• Keywords - a comma-separated list, e.g. “delivered, out for delivery”. Only notifications containing one of them (in the title, text or subtext, case-insensitive) are logged. Leave it empty to log every notification from that app.

• Notes - optional free text appended, on a new line, to the logged notification's text field. Useful for tagging a source, e.g. “work phone”. Notes are added even in metadata-only mode, since you wrote them yourself.

Excluded keywords under Privacy still win: a notification matching one is dropped regardless of these rules.
Some apps re-post the same notification repeatedly. “Ignore duplicate window” drops identical content from the same app seen within that many seconds (default one day). Set 0 to keep every copy.
Choose when uploads run: Periodic (every N minutes, min 15), Threshold (after N pending), or Manual (“Sync now” only). Optionally restrict to Wi-Fi or to charging to save battery/data.

Turn off “Capture notification body” to store metadata only. Add excluded keywords to drop notifications containing sensitive words (e.g. OTP). “Retention days” controls how long captured notification rows are kept before purging.

• 403 on upload: the auth header/token is wrong - for custom Header Auth use header name “key” and an empty prefix.\n• Nothing captured: grant notification access; check your included-apps selection.\n• Uploads delayed: allow the app to ignore battery optimization, or use “Sync now”.

This app is sideloaded and asks for SMS permissions on the companion, so Google Play Protect will warn on install and on some updates - that’s expected, not a sign of malware.

• On the prompt, tap “More details”, then “Install anyway”.
• If an update is blocked outright with a conflict error, that’s a signing mismatch, not Play Protect - uninstall the old build first (you’ll re-pair), then install the new one.
• On your own devices you can make updates apply silently over ADB (no fingerprint needed):
 adb shell settings put global verifier_verify_adb_installs 0
 adb install -r ariyipp.apk
For each app, log only the notifications containing one of the keywords. Leave keywords empty to log everything from that app. Notes are appended to the logged notification\'s text.
